simple.meaning: צָהֹב (tsâhôb) is a Hebrew word meaning “golden in color.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: צָהֹב (H6669) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Leviticus 13:30, with occurrences in Leviticus.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to צָהֹב (H6669) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in צָהֹב (H6669) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: צָהֹב (tsâhôb) / H6669 is traced through Leviticus 13:30, Leviticus 13:32, Leviticus 13:36 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: then the priest shall examine the plague; and behold, if its appearance is deeper than the skin, and the hair in it is yellow and thin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is an itch. It is leprosy of the head or of the beard.

timeline.evidenceText: then the priest shall examine the plague; and behold, if its appearance is deeper than the skin, and the hair in it is yellow and thin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is an itch. It is leprosy of the head or of the beard.
On the seventh day the priest shall examine the plague; and behold, if the itch hasn’t spread, and there is no yellow hair in it, and the appearance of the itch isn’t deeper than the skin,
then the priest shall examine him; and behold, if the itch has spread in the skin, the priest shall not look for the yellow hair; he is unclean.
